newsitem.title: USA: Top USDA officials before Senate on FY98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Top USDA officials before Senate on FY98 budget.

text.p: Top U.S. Agriculture Department officials Tuesday testified before a Senate subcommittee on the department's fiscal 1998 budget proposal and received a friendly reception from lawmakers.
The hearing by the Senate Appropriations subcommittee on agriculture focused mainly on recent food safety initiatives by the Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS).
Lawmakers also asked about a proposal for $390 million in user fees for meat inspection. Last week, panel chairman Thad Cochran, R-Miss., said the fees were not likely to be approved by Congress.
"I'm concerned we're moving more to a fee situation with our inspection services," said Sen. Conrad Burns, a Montana Republican. But Burns said he wanted to work with USDA on its fees.
Currently, industry pays unexpected over-time and holiday fees for government meat inspectors. The proposal would result in industry paying about 70 percent of the total cost.

"The administration believes that the collection of user fees is essential to the successful long-term implementation of meat, poultry and egg products inspection reforms," said FSIS administrator Thomas Billy.

Senators also pressed the Grain, Inspection, Packers and Stockyards Administration (GIPSA) on a request for $2.3 million to carry out the recommendations of a USDA panel on concentration in the livestock industry.
GIPSA Administrator James Baker said about one-third would be used to "better investigate" contract poultry production and the rest to refocus USDA's efforts on packer procurement.
"This is the third year we've asked for it, maybe the third year's a charm. We sure need more money," he told the panel.

Also testifying were Michael Dunn, Assistant Secretary of Agriculture for Marketing and Regulatory Programs, Lon Hatamiya, Administrator of the Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) and Terry Medley, Adminstrator of the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Services (APHIS).
The next hearing by the subcommittee on USDA's FY1998 budget is slated for March 11 on food and nutrition programs.
